p: and a place for gold where: His purpose is to declare that man may attain in this world to various secrets of nature, but man is never able to comprehend the wisdom of God.
and searcheth out all perfection: There is nothing but it is compassed within certain limits, and has an end, but God's wisdom.
inhabitant: Meaning, him that dwells by it.
bread: That is, come and underneath is brimstone or coal, which easily conceives fire.
of sapphires: He alludes to the mines and secrets of nature, which are under the earth, into which neither souls nor beasts can enter.
rock: After he has declared the wisdom of God in the secrets of nature he describes his power.
and where is the place of: Though God's power and wisdom may be understood in earthly things, yet his heavenly wisdom cannot be attained to.
the price thereof: It is too high a thing for man to attain to in this world.
gold: It can neither be bought for gold nor precious stones, but is only the gift of God.
pearls: Which was thought to be a king of precious stone.
fowls of the air: Meaning that there is no natural means by which man can attain heavenly wisdom: which he means by the souls, that fly high.
way thereof: He makes God the only author of this wisdom, and the giver of it.
fear of the Lord: He declares that man has as much of this heavenly wisdom as he shows by fearing God and departing from evil.
